lab01.title: Lab 01 — Meet the Course
lab01.html:
Lab 01 — Meet the Course

Category: Tuesday authenticated completion checkout, 25 or 0.

What today is: you get the course running and get your bearings. Nothing more. Every technical step happens together in class, click by click, with TAs in the rows. Thursday is the do lab — that is where you identify your target.

In class, together

  1. Meet your desk. Introduce yourself left and right; leave knowing at least two classmates. Partners are freely chosen and freely changed — your partner is your first line of support all semester.
  2. Tech gate, projected click by click. Open Colab (new notebook); sign in to ChatGPT and open Codex (the coding editor inside the same subscription — leave the tab open); sign in to Gemini; start the agy (Antigravity) installer — Gemini's coding editor, the only real install of the semester, started together so nobody fights it alone at home; upload and Run preflight_check.py. Green block = READY. Partner-verified, TA-confirmed; a failure is a support record, never a grade.
  3. Syllabus sprint — your first AI practice. Download the syllabus PDF from the Brightspace Syllabus tab; five minutes fast read; ask your partner one real question about the course; confirm the answer (or find it) with ChatGPT or Gemini — and point to the syllabus line that settles it. An AI answer counts only when the syllabus line backs it up. Unanswered questions go to the parking lot, answered Thursday.
  4. DRIVER first contact. The six stages in plain terms from the deck — you dominate the edges (define the question, explain the result), AI accelerates the middle. The 31-minute video deepens this before Thursday; today you only need the shape.
  5. One company you are curious about. Write one public company you would enjoy spending a semester understanding, and one sentence on why. This is curiosity, not analysis — Thursday turns curiosity into a defended choice.

Individual Brightspace checkout fields

  1. Lab Date (mm/dd/yyyy).
  2. Teammates / learning partners (Purdue usernames; worked individually is valid).
  3. Readiness record: READY with the preflight evidence, or RECOVERING with the exact error and the named next step + owner. Include: Codex tab opened yes/no; agy installed / still installing / blocked. (The shape, not your answer: "READY — preflight green in Colab, 126 rows AAPL, chart saved. Codex tab open. agy finished installing at 2:10.")
  4. Syllabus practice: your partner's question, the answer, and the syllabus line that settles it. (The shape, not your answer: "Q: can we drop a lab? A: yes — best-8-of-10 per category, syllabus 'Lab checkouts' paragraph.")
  5. DRIVER in your own words: one or two sentences — what belongs to you, what the AI accelerates.
  6. One company you are curious about and one sentence on why. Not graded for the choice — Asbury Automotive (ABG) is the instructor's demo and is off limits.
  7. Session token: the word announced in the room near the end of the session; it verifies your attendance attestation.
  8. Truth and in-person attendance attestation: "I attended this session in person and completed this checkout only for myself. I did not expose credentials."
  9. Receipt confirmation: submit and open the Brightspace attempt/receipt before leaving.

End with a growth note — two or three sentences, ungraded, for you alone: what can you do now that you could not do 75 minutes ago?

Completion standard

Full credit requires an on-time authenticated attempt that answers every field honestly. A documented technical failure with a named next step satisfies the readiness field — technology failure is never a finance-skill deficit here.

Before Thursday — do these:

  1. Watch the 31:07 DRIVER video (linked on the Week 1 page) — your only homework: own time, just watch, nothing to submit. Thursday's cases come from it. (Optional self-check: the 5-minute practice quiz.)
  2. Bring your working environment — or the exact error message and your named fix.

lab02.title: Lab 02 — Identify Your Target
lab02.html:
Lab 02 — Identify Your Target

Category: Thursday merit checkout, 0–25.

You arrive with: a working toolchain from Tuesday, one company you are curious about, and the DRIVER video watched — today's warm-up cases come from it. Today you identify your valuation target: the company that survives your own screen becomes your Project 1 company.

Mission

Act as an equity-research analyst deciding which public operating company deserves your next hundred hours. A composite score is not evidence by itself; the policy, the definitions, the data, one robustness test, and your judgment must agree. You are not proving the stock is attractive and you are not giving investment advice.

Training sequence

  1. Write your screening policy — AI off. Nine lines, solo (the deck carries a filled example of every line — the shape, not your answer): decision user · decision · universe · exclusions · two criteria · definitions · thresholds/weights · success test · one overriding disqualifier. Exclude banks, insurers, REITs, funds, shells, and other non-operating vehicles — the later Project 1 architecture is FCFF/enterprise-value based (FCFF = free cash flow to the firm; Week 2 teaches it with digits — for now it just means "an operating business we can value"). If you cannot name the fact that would kick your top company off the list, you do not have a policy — you have a mood.
  2. Run the two-AI comparison. One partner sends the same policy to ChatGPT, the other to Gemini (fallback: the Week 1 — Dual-System Output Packet in Start Here, or the COURSE-RUN PROBE: route from Start Here's AI Access page). Author one follow-up probe with your predicted answer written first. Mark one material suggestion accept, modify, reject, or unresolved. Two AIs agreeing is a coincidence of training data, not a fact about the world.
  3. Apply the policy. Implement your transparent rule in the downloaded screening_starter.py in Colab (or use the live instructor diagnostics / offline-screening-case.csv when network or provider fails — same finance either way). No silent definition changes.
  4. Validate — AI off. Check one load-bearing definition or company fact against provider documentation or a filing (the pre-staged Provider and Filing Definition Check keeps this bounded). Then run one ranking-stability change — one threshold, weight, lookback, or exclusion — and compare candidate order. No material change is a valid result when the test is genuine.
  5. Identify your target. Name the company, defend it to your partner in 45 seconds (six parts, example on the deck): target · two dated facts · most sensitive assumption · remaining unknown · decision · reversal trigger. A defensible no admissible target yet with a named next candidate is a strong outcome.

Individual Brightspace checkout fields

  1. Lab Date (mm/dd/yyyy).
  2. Teammates and personal contribution.
  3. Problem and decision: decision user, universe, exclusions, and what the screen selects for.
  4. Your screening policy: the nine lines, written before AI.
  5. AI-use record: named access path; your probe and prior prediction; one suggestion accepted/modified/rejected/unresolved and why. (The shape, not your answer: "ChatGPT web + Gemini web. Probe: which criterion is most sensitive to the three-year lookback? Predicted volatility; both returned volatility. Accepted Gemini's suggestion to state the lookback in the definition.")
  6. Data and evidence: source/provider, returned period and as-of date (or the exact offline-case label), and the candidate comparison. (The shape, not your answer: "yfinance via the starter, 3y daily adjusted prices, as of 08/27/2026; top three under my policy were A, B, C.")
  7. Independent validation: the definition/fact checked, source and date, and your accept/qualify/reject conclusion.
  8. Stability test: the changed input, original vs revised order, and what it means economically.
  9. Your target: company/ticker; the material unknown; and the observable disqualifier or reversal trigger. (The shape, not your answer — training case: "MSFT; unknown: the five-year window is untested; reversal: volatility above my 0.25 ceiling on the longer window.")
  10. Optional artifact link when a durable notebook/repository exists.
  11. Session token — announced in the room near the end of the session.
  12. Truth and in-person attendance attestation.
  13. Receipt confirmation: submit and open the receipt before leaving.

End with a growth note — ungraded, yours alone.

Merit anchors — 5 points each

Merit anchors — 5 points each
Criterion 5 — strong observable evidence 3 — usable but incomplete 0–1 — not demonstrated
Problem and decision specific user, universe, exclusions, success test usable decision with one vague boundary generic "best stock" or no research gate
Policy before AI nine lines, defensible disqualifier, written pre-AI policy exists, one element missing or post-hoc criteria came from AI
Data and evidence integrity dated sources, definitions, traceable output one minor traceability gap untraceable ranking or mixed definitions
Validation and robustness genuine source check + interpreted stability test checks exist, one mechanical AI agreement treated as validation
Judgment and explanation target follows evidence; unknown + trigger named; clear 45-second defense defensible target, vague condition unsupported buy claim or score treated as truth

Intermediate anchors: 4 = one minor non-load-bearing weakness; 2 = an important link incomplete; 1 = minimal attempt; 0 = missing or fabricated. Do not award points for confidence, effort, or speaking style.

Before Tuesday — do these:

  1. Watch the 23-minute three-lens video (linked on the Week 2 page) — the template for everything you build in Weeks 2–4.
  2. Save your target's latest primary filing (10-K or 10-Q) where you can open it in class.
  3. Write one sentence: the decision this valuation will support, and for whom.

Lab 03 preview: write your before-AI valuation baseline — Project 1 Edition A, the frozen proof that the judgment in this project is yours.

p1.html:
Project 1 — Corporate Finance Application

Role and committee decision

You are the AI task force member embedded in a buy-side analyst group. The fund holds no position in your target company. The senior analysts own the sector view; you were brought in to do what your generation of analysts does best — build the evidence-and-model stack with AI acceleration, faster and more transparently than it has ever been built, without ever letting the machine own the judgment. The portfolio manager's ask: should the fund initiate a position, place the name on watch/defer, or do not initiate — delivered as a defensible valuation range with evidence dates, material conditions, and reversal/monitoring triggers, never a single confident number. Your group will challenge your assumptions before the committee does; the committee sees your memo and your recorded defense. Screening selected the research target; it is not valuation evidence and cannot determine the recommendation.

Points and the enforced due date appear in the Brightspace assignment header. The separate Project 1 — Edition A Checkpoint (AI Closed) page publishes the supervised baseline window; do not use the final-assignment page as the Edition A submission location.

Planning estimate: 18–25 hours distributed across Weeks 2–8, including research, modeling, validation, cold run, writing, recording, transcript correction, and access checks.

Role and committee decision
Week Project 1 planning band Scope boundary
2 3–4 h Edition A, source map, valuation architecture
3 3–4 h FCFF/WACC/terminal model and validation
4 3–4 h peer policy, multiples, transaction qualification
5 3–4 h pro-forma build: personalized drivers, five-year statements, articulation checks
6 3–4 h assumption research and challenges; sensitivity/what-if incl. a downside case; fresh-eyes revision; decision range
7 2.5–4 h cold run, manifest, memo, three bounded recordings
8 0.5–1 h access/integrity check and final receipt; no new analysis

Required finance system

Build a locally runnable analysis/application that:

  1. identifies the intended investment user, decision horizon, target/security, valuation date, currency, share basis (basic vs. diluted count), and relevant exclusions;
  2. traces material historical inputs to filings or authoritative sources and distinguishes facts, normalizations, forecasts, and model outputs — including a base year normalized for one-time items and basis changes (the Week 2 contamination catalog);
  3. builds a five-year three-statement pro-forma (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow) with a driver architecture personalized to the company — pro-forma is a method, not an algorithm; every load-bearing driver carries value · basis · challenge · evidence that would change it — and statements that articulate under checks that can fail loudly (balance sheet balances every year, cash flow ties to balance-sheet cash, base year reconciles to the filing);
  4. constructs the five-year FCFF DCF with WACC, terminal convention, and a complete enterprise-to-equity/per-share bridge — built as an engine in Week 3, then driven by the pro-forma's operating forecast from Week 5 on;
  5. reports causal low/base/high cases, a WACC–growth sensitivity, terminal-value share, and one reverse-DCF or market-implied expectation;
  6. defines a comparable-company policy before selecting peers and calculates at least one consistent enterprise-value and one equity-value multiple; use relevant transaction evidence only when its control/synergy/time context can be defended;
  7. explains disagreement across methods rather than mechanically averaging them;
  8. stresses the pro-forma with named what-if scenarios, including at least one downside case that could alter the recommendation, and maintains an assumption-challenge record (each load-bearing driver: value · basis · challenge · evidence that would change it); partner fresh-eyes challenges from the Weeks 5–6 labs belong in this record, credited to the challenger; and
  9. produces a valuation range and conditional committee action, not false point precision.

Because the required architecture is enterprise-value/FCFF, banks, insurers, REITs, and other issuers for which FCFF and an enterprise-to-equity bridge are economically inappropriate are not eligible Project 1 targets. Select another operating company by the Week 2 admission gate. Such issuers may be used later only when an approved project architecture fits the decision.

All market facts carry source and as-of date. Provider labels are reconciled to definitions. The repository must show the material inputs and result without requiring a grader to run it.

Edition A boundary

Submit the designated Brightspace Edition A checkpoint during Week 2 before valuation-specific generative-AI research or coding. The first successful receipt is the baseline of record; a Git tag may corroborate history but cannot replace the Brightspace checkpoint. Week 1's disclosed AI-assisted screening occurred before this project boundary; Edition A captures the student's valuation judgment before valuation-specific AI assistance.

Required validation

  • one synthetic/known-answer reconciliation (against the training-case answers published with the weekly starters);
  • one independent source/definition check on a load-bearing input;
  • one directional changed-input test written before execution;
  • one Locked Changed-Input Record with a human-authored, AI-off prediction before the run, precommit timestamp/commit, old/new input and units, expected/actual output direction, decision effect, and failure diagnosis or no-change reason;
  • pro-forma articulation checks (balance sheet balances; cash flow ties to cash; base-year reconciliation to the filing), DCF boundary/monotonicity checks (outputs move only in the expected direction as WACC or growth moves), and enterprise-equity bridge checks;
  • peer-policy and multiple-definition consistency check;
  • highest-risk failure test plus cold-run log (one clean end-to-end run in a fresh environment, recorded); and
  • one accepted, corrected, qualified, or rejected AI output with independent evidence.

Submission and scoring

Submit the uniform seven-part bundle and filenames in the shared checklist: unchanged Edition A plus Edition B, repository/visible output, research-evolution Video 1, code/validation Video 2, memo/deck, and committee Video 3 with corrected transcripts and frozen validation/AI-use record. The 300-point mapping in the major-project analytic rubric applies. No extra points attach to number of commits, visual polish, framework vocabulary, or video existence.

Before grading, Brightspace also publishes Project 1 — Annotated Decision-Evidence Excerpt and Non-Example. It illustrates observable decision-evidence anchors and common failures but is not a complete submission, model answer, or source of project facts.
